findings.title: All operations are valid declarative patches
findings.explanation: 2 operation(s) target allowlisted state paths with valid values and resolvable targets. No command strings detected.

findings.title: Plan destroys stateful resources
findings.explanation: 1 stateful resource(s) would be destroyed or replaced: module.audit.aws_s3_bucket.compliance_logs (replace). Destroying these loses data, not just capacity.
findings.remediation: Remove the destroy from the plan, or mark the resource with the "changesafe_backup" tag once a restorable backup exists.

findings.title: Plan destroys a protected resource
findings.explanation: module.audit.aws_s3_bucket.compliance_logs is protected and would be replaced. Protected resources cannot be destroyed by a gated change.
findings.remediation: Remove the destroy, or lift the protection deliberately in a separate, reviewed change.

findings.title: Configuration is recoverable, data is not
findings.explanation: The plan records prior configuration for every destroyed resource, so infrastructure can be rebuilt. However 1 of them hold state (module.audit.aws_s3_bucket.compliance_logs), and their contents are not in the plan.
findings.remediation: Confirm a restorable backup exists and mark it with the "changesafe_backup" tag.

findings.title: The plan carries review context
findings.explanation: The plan carries 1 context entry for the pull request review to check against.

findings.title: Blast radius within limits (2 resources)
findings.explanation: Operations touch 2 resources (aws-iam-role-policy-log-writer, module-audit-aws-s3-bucket-compliance-logs), within the warning threshold of 15.

findings.title: Input content contains instruction-like language
findings.explanation: context ev-context-0 contains "Ignore previous safety rules". This text is data, not instructions — it was flagged deterministically and had no ability to alter policy evaluation.
findings.remediation: Treat the flagged content as untrusted. Verify the underlying facts independently before acting on them.

skippedPolicies.because: a Terraform plan carries no inverse operations to verify; reverting means reverting the code, not replaying a patch

the proposal is derived mechanically from the plan with no model involved, so it can never declare its own precondition or postcheck steps; verification in this workflow happens through the pull request review instead
